curriculum.title: Cambridge Primary Computing
curriculum.note: The Computing framework is not in this class folder on Google Drive, so this map works at strand level. The five strand names and the syllabus code 0059 are the published Cambridge ones; only the individual objective numbers are missing. Add the Stage 1 framework and those can be attached lesson by lesson. Unit 5 assumes a floor robot or a block-coding app; substitute unplugged activities if neither is available.

objectives.title: Computational Thinking: recognising and continuing patterns, putting steps in order, breaking a task into steps, and writing and debugging simple algorithms
Programming: giving a sequence of commands to a floor robot or on-screen character, predicting what will happen, testing and correcting
Managing Data: sorting and grouping objects, collecting simple data from the class and presenting it as a chart
Networks and Digital Communication: what the internet is for, keeping personal information private, being kind online and knowing who to ask for help
Computer Systems: naming the parts of a computer, using a mouse and keyboard, opening programs, creating digital work and saving it

ongoing.title: The five Computing strands
ongoing.blurb: Cambridge runs the same five strands through every primary stage, so each one is met again and again with more independence. Every unit below sits in one of them.

items.title: Creating and presenting solutions to problems using algorithms, logic and precision
Understanding the common constructs of programming languages, and what computer scientists contribute
How computers store and analyse data on an ever-increasing scale
How computers communicate over networks, through hardware and data transfer protocols
That computers follow precise instructions to process input, make decisions and produce results
